title: Number of Perfect Pairs
summary: Given an integer array, count the number of distinct pairs (i, j) where i < j, and the indices satisfy specific conditions involving the absolute values of the elements at those indices.
statement: Given an integer array, count the number of distinct pairs (i, j) where i < j, and the indices satisfy specific conditions involving the absolute values of the elements at those indices.
constraints: The array has between two and 100,000 signed integers.
For each i<j, test both |a-b| and |a+b| against the smaller and larger magnitudes.
Return the number of qualifying index pairs.
reference_solution:
def count_perfect_pairs(nums):
    values=sorted(abs(value) for value in nums);zeros=0
    while zeros<len(values) and values[zeros]==0:zeros+=1
    answer=zeros*(zeros-1)//2;left=zeros
    for right in range(zeros,len(values)):
        while left<right and values[right]>2*values[left]:left+=1
        answer+=right-left
    return answer

hints: For magnitudes x<=y, the two expressions are y-x and y+x regardless of signs.
The second inequality is automatic; the first becomes y<=2x, with zero pairing only with zero.
Sort absolute values, count zero-zero pairs, and use a moving left boundary for each positive right endpoint.
All indices from the first magnitude at least half of y through right-1 qualify, and monotonic sorting makes the boundary move only forward.
editorial: All indices from the first magnitude at least half of y through right-1 qualify, and monotonic sorting makes the boundary move only forward.

tests.explanation: Only magnitude pairs one-two and two-three satisfy the inequalities.
Four index pairs have larger magnitude at most twice the smaller magnitude.
